s92-lims-001.text: In the normal (non-degraded) AFCS configuration for IFR or VFR operations (PSAS1 and PSAS2, AP1 and AP2, ATT Mode), what is the maximum VNE? -- Correct: 165 KIAS. With the full normal AFCS configuration engaged (PSAS1/2, AP1/2, ATT Mode, cyclic and rudder trim), maximum VNE is 165 KIAS — and it stays 165 KIAS with just one AP, or in SAS Mode, as long as both PSAS1 and PSAS2 are still operating. VNE drops to 120 KIAS only when a single PSAS channel is paired with both APs in ATT Mode, or when a single PSAS/AP pair operates in SAS Mode.
s92-lims-001.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I REQUIRED EQUIPMENT p.1-1/1-2 (AFCS config table): full config 165 KIAS; one AP or SAS Mode with both PSAS1+PSAS2 still 165 KIAS; single PSAS paired with both APs in ATT, or single PSAS/AP pair in SAS, drops to 120 KIAS. Explanation corrected in this pass to match the table precisely (previous text wrongly said 'SAS Mode or a single AP reduces to 120'). Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-002.text: What is the minimum flight crew specified in the S-92 RFM? -- Correct: Two pilots. The RFM specifies a minimum flight crew of two pilots; the Pilot in Command may occupy either cockpit seat.
s92-lims-002.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I MINIMUM FLIGHT CREW p.1-2: 'Minimum flight crew is two pilots.' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-003.text: What limitation applies to the Enhanced Ground Proximity Warning System (EGPWS)? -- Correct: Navigation must not be predicated upon the use of EGPWS information. The EGPWS does not include power lines in its database, so navigation must never be predicated upon EGPWS information; the terrain/obstacle display is an awareness tool only, not a routine navigation reference.
s92-lims-003.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I EGPWS p.1-2: 'Navigation must not be predicated upon the use of EGPWS information.' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-004.text: For RNP5/BRNAV operation with the FMS, usable navigation information must be received from which source(s)? -- Correct: GPS, or one VOR/DME, or multiple DMEs. RNP5/BRNAV is approved provided the FMS receives usable navigation information from GPS, or from one VOR/DME, or from multiple DMEs.
s92-lims-004.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I FMS OPERATIONAL APPROVALS p.1-3: RNP5/BRNAV requires GPS, or one VOR/DME, or multiple DMEs. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-005.text: Which of the following is explicitly prohibited under FLIGHT LIMITS in the S-92 RFM? -- Correct: Practice touchdown autorotations. FLIGHT LIMITS explicitly prohibits practice touchdown autorotations, along with aerobatic maneuvers and 360° hovering turns in less than 12 seconds.
s92-lims-005.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I FLIGHT LIMITS p.1-5: practice touchdown autorotations explicitly prohibited. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-006.text: What is the maximum crosswind component for Category A ground level helipad takeoffs and landings? -- Correct: 22 knots. Category A ground level helipad takeoffs and landings are limited to 22 knots of crosswind component; Category A horizontal takeoffs and landings allow up to 35 knots.
s92-lims-006.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I FLIGHT LIMITS p.1-5: Category A ground level helipad crosswind 22 kt; horizontal takeoff/landing crosswind 35 kt. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-007.text: What is the maximum bank angle permitted with one primary flight control servo inoperative? -- Correct: 30°. With one primary flight control servo inoperative, maximum bank angle is limited to 30°.
s92-lims-007.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I FLIGHT LIMITS p.1-5: max bank angle with one primary flight control servo inoperative is 30°. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-008.text: With low fuel light(s) illuminated, which steady-state pitch attitudes must be avoided? -- Correct: More than 10° nose up or more than 5° nose down. With low fuel light(s) illuminated, the RFM directs avoiding steady state pitch attitudes in excess of 10° nose up and lower than 5° nose down.
s92-lims-008.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I FLIGHT LIMITS p.1-5: with low fuel light(s) illuminated, avoid pitch >10° nose up or >5° nose down. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-009.text: What are the slope landing limits stated in the S-92 RFM? -- Correct: 10° nose up or down slope, 13° left or right side up-slope. Slope landing limits are 10° nose up or down slope, and 13° left or right side of the aircraft up-slope.
s92-lims-009.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I FLIGHT LIMITS p.1-5: slope landing limits 10° nose/tail up-slope, 13° left/right up-slope. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-010.text: If VNE power on is less than 120 KIAS, what VNE power off value applies? -- Correct: The lower VNE power-on value applies for the power-off case as well. VNE power off is normally 120 KIAS, but if VNE power on is less than 120 KIAS, that lower value applies for the power-off case as well.
s92-lims-010.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I AIRSPEED LIMITS p.1-7: VNE power off 120 KIAS, or the lower VNE power-on value if that is less than 120 KIAS. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-011.text: What is the maximum airspeed with one engine inoperative? -- Correct: 120 KIAS. Maximum airspeed with one engine inoperative is 120 KIAS, the same limit that applies with SAS, AP, or primary flight control servo degradations.
s92-lims-011.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I AIRSPEED LIMITS p.1-7: 'Maximum airspeed with one engine inoperative is 120 KIAS.' Confirmed on the rendered page image (same page also confirms one/both SAS inoperative, both APs inoperative, and one primary flight control servo inoperative are all separately listed at 120 KIAS).

s92-lims-012.text: What is the maximum airspeed with the hydraulic boost system inoperative? -- Correct: 120 KIAS. Maximum airspeed with the hydraulic boost inoperative is 120 KIAS.
s92-lims-012.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I AIRSPEED LIMITS p.1-7: 'Maximum airspeed with the hydraulic boost inoperative is 120 KIAS.' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-013.text: What is the maximum groundspeed for taxi operations and for brake application? -- Correct: 35 knots. Maximum groundspeed for taxi operations is 35 knots, and maximum groundspeed for brake application is also 35 knots.
s92-lims-013.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I AIRSPEED LIMITS p.1-7/1-8: 'Maximum groundspeed for taxi operations is 35 knots. Maximum groundspeed for brake application is 35 knots.' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-014.text: What is the maximum enroute altitude limit stated under ALTITUDE LIMITS? -- Correct: 15,000 feet density altitude. Enroute altitude is limited to 15,000 feet density altitude. Flight in icing conditions with RIPS installed is limited to 10,000 feet pressure altitude, a separate limit.
s92-lims-014.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I ALTITUDE LIMITS p.1-8: 'Enroute: 15,000 feet density altitude.' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-015.text: What is the ambient temperature operating range for the S-92 per AMBIENT TEMPERATURE LIMITS? -- Correct: -40°C to ISA +35°C. The ambient temperature operating range is -40°C to ISA +35°C. Operation is also prohibited if the shut-down rotorcraft is exposed below -25°C for longer than 1 hour without warming or use of the cold weather pre-heat kit.
s92-lims-015.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I AMBIENT TEMPERATURE LIMITS p.1-8: '-40°C to ISA +35°C.' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-016.text: What is the maximum takeoff and landing weight of the S-92 per Part 1 WEIGHT LIMITS? -- Correct: 26,500 pounds. Maximum takeoff and landing weight is 26,500 pounds (12,020 kilograms); minimum operating weight is 16,200 pounds.
s92-lims-016.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I WEIGHT LIMITS p.1-9: 'Maximum takeoff and landing weight is 26,500 pounds (12,020 kilograms).' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-017.text: What is the maximum continuous torque (Q%) rating for dual-engine operation? -- Correct: 100%. Dual-engine maximum continuous torque is 100% Q. 120% Q is the single-engine (OEI) maximum continuous rating, and 141% Q is the OEI 30-second rating — not the dual-engine continuous value.
s92-lims-017.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I PROPULSION AND DRIVE SYSTEM LIMITS p.1-18 (CT7-8A master table): dual-engine maximum continuous torque 100% Q. Confirmed on the rendered page image (already read while sourcing s92-lims-040/041 in the prior session).

s92-lims-018.text: What is the single-engine (OEI) 30-second torque limit? -- Correct: 141%. The OEI 30-second torque limit is 141% Q. 120% Q is OEI maximum continuous, and 156% Q is the OEI 5-second transient limit.
s92-lims-018.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I PROPULSION AND DRIVE SYSTEM LIMITS p.1-18 (CT7-8A master table): single-engine OEI transient 5 sec 156(3)% Q. Confirmed correct on the rendered page image in the prior session (initially suspected wrong due to an unrelated similarly-numbered value on p.1-23, ruled a false alarm after finding the specific master-table row).

s92-lims-019.text: Which Np/Nr ranges must be avoided for prolonged operation per the RFM? -- Correct: 36% to 49%, and 56% to 67%. Prolonged operation must be avoided in the 36% to 49% Np/Nr range (tail rotor drive shaft critical range) and the 56% to 67% range (engine power turbine critical range).
s92-lims-019.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I Np/Nr AVOID RANGES p.1-18: avoid 36-49% and 56-67% Np/Nr for prolonged operation. Confirmed on the rendered page image in the prior session.

s92-lims-020.text: Under FUEL CROSSFEED LIMITS, when is fuel crossfeed permitted for Category A operations? -- Correct: Emergency operation only. Fuel crossfeed for Category A operations is limited to emergency operation only. Category B fuel crossfeed is limited to cruise flight only — a distinct, category-specific limit.
s92-lims-020.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I FUEL CROSSFEED LIMITS p.1-19: 'Category A - emergency operation only. Category B - cruise flight only.' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-021.text: Per FUEL TEMPERATURE LIMITS, what is the maximum permitted fuel temperature for Jet A (JP-5, No. 3 Jet Fuel) or Jet A-1 (JP-8)? -- Correct: 57°C (135°F). Jet A and Jet A-1 have a maximum fuel temperature of 57°C (135°F). Jet B (JP-4) is lower, at 16°C (60°F); all three fuels share the same minimum of -40°C (-40°F).
s92-lims-021.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I FUEL TEMPERATURE LIMITS p.1-20: Jet A/Jet A-1 max 57C(135F) min -40C; Jet B max 16C(60F) min -40C. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-022.text: At what fuel temperature does FUEL TEMPERATURE LIMITS require a fuel anti-icing additive? -- Correct: Below -20°C (-4°F). Fuel anti-icing additives are required at fuel temperatures below -20°C (-4°F); above that threshold, heating or anti-icing additive is not required.
s92-lims-022.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I FUEL TEMPERATURE LIMITS p.1-20: 'Fuel anti-icing additives are required at fuel temperatures below -20C (-4F).' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-023.text: What is the total fuel quantity for a gravity refuel, per FUEL CAPACITY? -- Correct: 713 US gallons (2700 L). Gravity refuel total capacity is 713 US gallons (2700 liters); pressure refuel is higher, at 764 US gallons (2890 liters). Of the total quantity, 4.8 gallons (18 liters) is unusable.
s92-lims-023.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I FUEL CAPACITY p.1-20: Gravity refuel 713 US gal/2700L; Pressure refuel 764 US gal/2890L; 4.8 gal/18L unusable. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-024.text: Why does the RFM recommend servicing engines only with approved Type II oils rather than Type I? -- Correct: Type II oils withstand higher operating temperatures and have improved anti-coking characteristics. Type II oils can withstand higher operating temperatures and have improved anti-coking characteristics. They also have higher viscosity than Type I, which may result in slightly higher oil pressure under similar speed/temperature conditions — the opposite of "lower viscosity, reduces pressure."
s92-lims-024.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I APPROVED OILS p.1-21: 'Type II oils...can withstand higher operating temperatures...improved anti-coking characteristics. Type II oils have higher viscosity than Type I that may result in slightly higher oil pressure.' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-025.text: According to APPROVED OILS, is mixing Type I and Type II engine oils authorized? -- Correct: Yes, though it is recommended to use only one type when possible. The RFM authorizes mixing of brand names as well as mixing of Type I and Type II oils, while recommending that only one type be used when possible.
s92-lims-025.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I APPROVED OILS p.1-21: 'The mixing of brand name as well as the mixing of Type I and Type II oils is authorized. It is recommended that only one type of oil be used when possible.' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-026.text: Per BACK-TO-BACK STARTING LIMIT, above +15°C (+59°F), what starting cycle is permitted before a 30-minute cooling period is required? -- Correct: 2 consecutive starts, 5-minute cooling, then 2 more consecutive starts. Above +15°C (+59°F): 2 consecutive starts, 5-minute cooling, 2 more consecutive starts, then a 30-minute cooling period before repeating. At +15°C or below, the limit is more permissive: 4 starts, 15-minute cooling, 4 more starts, then 30 minutes.
s92-lims-026.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I STARTER LIMITS, BACK-TO-BACK STARTING LIMIT p.1-22: >+15C: 2 starts/5min cooling/2 starts/30min cooling/repeat. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-027.text: At or below +15°C (+59°F), how many consecutive engine starts are permitted before a 15-minute cooling period, per BACK-TO-BACK STARTING LIMIT? -- Correct: 4. At +15°C (+59°F) or less, the cycle is 4 consecutive starts, 15-minute cooling, 4 more consecutive starts, then 30-minute cooling, then repeat.
s92-lims-027.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I STARTER LIMITS, BACK-TO-BACK STARTING LIMIT p.1-22: <=+15C: 4 starts/15min cooling/4 starts/30min cooling/repeat. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-028.text: What is the STARTER MOTORING LIMIT cycle? -- Correct: 2 minutes on, 5 minutes off, 2 minutes on, 30 minutes off, then repeat. Starter motoring limit is 2 minutes on / 5 minutes off, then 2 minutes on / 30 minutes off, then the cycle repeats.
s92-lims-028.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I STARTER MOTORING LIMIT p.1-22: 2min on/5min off/2min on/30min off/repeat. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-029.text: Per ENGINE AND APU INFLIGHT STARTING, APU starts and continuous operation in flight are restricted to airspeeds below what value? -- Correct: 150 KIAS. Engine starts in flight are authorized throughout the complete aircraft operating envelope, but APU starts and continuous APU operation are restricted to airspeeds less than 150 KIAS.
s92-lims-029.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I ENGINE AND APU INFLIGHT STARTING p.1-22: 'APU starts and continuous operation are restricted to airspeeds less than 150 KIAS.' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-030.text: What is the maximum MGB oil temperature, per MGB OIL TEMPERATURE LIMITS? -- Correct: 130°C. MGB oil temperature: continuous 0° to 120°C, precautionary 120° to 130°C, maximum 130°C. Don't confuse it with the separate engine oil temperature limits (continuous to 132°C, maximum 149°C).
s92-lims-030.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I MGB OIL TEMPERATURE LIMITS p.1-23: Continuous 0-120C, Precautionary 120-130C, Maximum 130C (cross-checked against engine oil temp 132/149C on the same page to confirm they are distinct systems). Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-031.text: With Nr at or above 80%, or the aircraft airborne, what is the minimum MGB oil pressure per MGB OIL PRESSURE LIMITS? -- Correct: 35 psi. With Nr ≥ 80% or the aircraft in the air: minimum 35 psi, precautionary 35–45 psi, continuous 45–70 psi, precautionary 70–130 psi, maximum 130 psi. The minimum is lower (10 psi) only in the two ground-operation, lower-Nr conditions.
s92-lims-031.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I MGB OIL PRESSURE LIMITS p.1-23: Condition Nr>=80% or airborne: Min 35psi, Precautionary 35-45, Continuous 45-70, Precautionary 70-130, Max 130. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-032.text: What is the normal operating rotor speed range (power on) for dual-engine operation, per ROTOR SPEED LIMITS? -- Correct: 104% to 106%. Power-on normal operating rotor speed is 104% to 106% for dual engine, and 100% to 106% for OEI — two distinct ranges depending on engine state.
s92-lims-032.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I ROTOR SPEED LIMITS, POWER ON p.1-24: Normal dual-engine 104-106%, Normal OEI 100-106%. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-033.text: What are the power-on OEI rotor speed transient limits? -- Correct: 90% transient minimum; 80% transient at touchdown during an OEI landing. Power-on: transient minimum OEI is 90%, and transient at touchdown during an OEI landing is 80% — a lower, specifically-carved-out allowance for that one phase of flight.
s92-lims-033.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I ROTOR SPEED LIMITS, POWER ON p.1-24: Transient minimum OEI 90%, Transient at touchdown during OEI landing 80%. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-034.text: At what power-off rotor speed does the minimum threshold ("LOW ROTOR" aural alert) occur? -- Correct: 95%. Power off: maximum 110%, minimum ("LOW ROTOR" aural alert) 95%, transient minimum 80%.
s92-lims-034.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I ROTOR SPEED LIMITS, POWER OFF p.1-24: Maximum 110%, Minimum (LOW ROTOR aural alert) 95%, Transient minimum 80%. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-035.text: What must be done before applying the rotor brake, per the ROTOR TURNING CAUTION? -- Correct: Both engines must be shut down. CAUTION: both engines must be shut down before applying the rotor brake.
s92-lims-035.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I ROTOR BRAKE LIMITS, ROTOR TURNING p.1-25 CAUTION: 'Both engines must be shut down before applying the rotor brake.' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-036.text: What is the maximum rotor speed for an EMERGENCY rotor brake application, with both engines shut down? -- Correct: 105% Nr. Recommended rotor speed for a normal rotor brake application is 40% Nr or below; the maximum rotor speed for an emergency rotor brake application, with both engines shut down, is 105% Nr.
s92-lims-036.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I ROTOR BRAKE LIMITS, ROTOR TURNING p.1-25: 'Recommended rotor speed for normal rotor brake application is 40% Nr or below. Maximum rotor speed for emergency rotor brake application with both engines shut down is 105% Nr.' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-037.text: What is the normal operating pressure range for the S-92 hydraulic system, per HYDRAULIC SYSTEM LIMITS? -- Correct: 3500 to 4200 psi. Hydraulic system limits: depress (System 3 only) 2000 ± 1000 psi, minimum 3500 psi, normal 3500 to 4200 psi, maximum 4200 psi.
s92-lims-037.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I HYDRAULIC SYSTEM LIMITS p.1-25: Depress(sys3 only) 2000+/-1000psi, Minimum 3500psi, Normal 3500-4200psi, Maximum 4200psi. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-038.text: Per APPROVED HYDRAULIC FLUID, what restriction applies to MIL-PRF-83282 fluid? -- Correct: It may only be used at ambient temperatures above -32°C (-25°F). MIL-PRF-87257 is authorized at all approved ambient temperatures; MIL-PRF-83282 may only be used at ambient temperatures above -32°C (-25°F).
s92-lims-038.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I APPROVED HYDRAULIC FLUID p.1-25: 'MIL-PRF-87257 is authorized for use at all approved ambient temperatures. MIL-PRF-83282 may only be used at ambient temperatures above -32C (-25F).' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-039.text: Per the INSTRUMENT MARKINGS for engine oil pressure, what is the idle minimum pressure band? -- Correct: 20 to 30 psi. Engine oil pressure markings: 120 psi maximum, 100–120 psi 5-minute band, 30–100 psi continuous, and 20–30 psi idle minimum.
s92-lims-039.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I INSTRUMENT MARKINGS, Figure 1-6 Sheet 1 p.1-26: Engine oil pressure 120psi max/100-120 5min/30-100 continuous/20-30 idle minimum. Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-040.text: Maximum continuous dual-engine torque may exceed 100% on one engine up to what maximum, provided the sum of both engines' torque does not exceed 200%? -- Correct: 110%, provided the other engine's torque is proportionally less than 100%. Maximum continuous dual-engine torque may exceed 100% on one engine to a maximum of 110%, provided the torque on the other engine is proportionally less than 100% and the sum of the individual torque values does not exceed 200%.
s92-lims-040.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I PROPULSION AND DRIVE SYSTEM LIMITS p.1-18, table note: 'Maximum continuous dual engine torque may exceed 100% on one engine to a maximum of 110% provided that the torque on the other engine is proportionally less than 100% and the sum of the individual torque values does not exceed 200%.' Confirmed on the rendered page image (CT7-8A master limits table).

s92-lims-041.text: At airspeeds greater than 100 KIAS, dual-engine maximum continuous torque is reduced from 100% to 86% Q. Why? -- Correct: To limit flight control loads at high speed and preserve dynamic component replacement times — it is explicitly not a gearbox limit. Table note (1): "86% Q is not a gearbox limit. Its purpose is to limit flight control loads at high speed thereby preserving dynamic component replacement times."
s92-lims-041.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I PROPULSION AND DRIVE SYSTEM LIMITS p.1-18, note (1): '86% Q is not a gearbox limit. Its purpose is to limit flight control loads at high speed thereby preserving dynamic component replacement times.' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-042.text: What is the 5-minute takeoff TGT limit for dual-engine operation, and how does it compare to maximum continuous? -- Correct: 995°C for 5 minutes, versus 935°C maximum continuous. Dual-engine TGT: maximum continuous 935°C, 30-minute (hover only) 988°C, takeoff (5 min) 995°C, transient (12 sec) 1003°C.
s92-lims-042.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I PROPULSION AND DRIVE SYSTEM LIMITS p.1-18 (CT7-8A master table): Dual engine TGT max continuous 935C, takeoff(5min) 995C. Cross-checked against INSTRUMENT MARKINGS Sheet 5 p.1-30 (995C-5min/988C-30min/935C max continuous gauge markings). Confirmed on rendered page images.

s92-lims-043.text: What is the single-engine (OEI) 30-second TGT limit? -- Correct: 1049°C. Single-engine TGT: maximum continuous 988°C, OEI 2-minute 1006°C, OEI 30-second 1049°C, maximum starting (peak) 1000°C.
s92-lims-043.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I PROPULSION AND DRIVE SYSTEM LIMITS p.1-18 (CT7-8A master table): Single engine OEI TGT 30sec 1049C, 2min 1006C, max continuous 988C. Cross-checked against INSTRUMENT MARKINGS Sheet 5 p.1-30. Confirmed on rendered page images.

s92-lims-044.text: At what Np and Ng values do the automatic overspeed trips activate, per the PROPULSION AND DRIVE SYSTEM LIMITS notes? -- Correct: Np at 120%, Ng at 108.5%. "Np overspeed trip is at 120%. Ng overspeed trip is at 108.5%." These are automatic protective trips, distinct from the normal rated Np/Ng operating values in the same table.
s92-lims-044.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I PROPULSION AND DRIVE SYSTEM LIMITS p.1-18, table notes: 'Np overspeed trip is at 120%. Ng overspeed trip is at 108.5%.' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-045.text: What is the maximum allowable cabin floor loading, and how does a heavy-duty floor change it? -- Correct: 75 lb/sq ft (366 kg/m²) standard, 200 lb/sq ft (976 kg/m²) with a heavy-duty floor. Maximum allowable cabin floor loading is 75 lb/sq ft (366 kg/m²); with a heavy-duty floor installed, it rises to 200 lb/sq ft (976 kg/m²).
s92-lims-045.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I CABIN FLOOR LOADING LIMITS p.1-17: 'Maximum allowable cabin floor loading is 75 pounds per square foot (366 Kg per square meter). If the helicopter is equipped with a heavy duty floor, the maximum loading is 200 pounds per square foot (976 Kg per square meter).' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-046.text: With the rear ramp area configured for stowing baggage, what is the maximum combined load, and the maximum shelf load? -- Correct: 1,000 lb (454 kg) combined; 300 lb (136 kg) maximum shelf load. With the aft cabin cargo bulkhead and shelf installed, the maximum combined load is 1,000 lb (454 kg); the maximum shelf load is 300 lb (136 kg); the maximum floor ramp load is also 1,000 lb (454 kg), at up to 200 lb/sq ft (976.5 kg/m²).
s92-lims-046.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I BAGGAGE LOADING LIMIT p.1-17: 'maximum combined load is 1,000 pounds (454 kilograms). The maximum shelf load is 300 pounds (136 kilograms).' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-047.text: Per the CAUTION preceding CABIN FLOOR LOADING LIMITS, a fuel-tank imbalance in excess of what value — combined with grossly unbalanced cargo/passenger loading — may put the aircraft outside allowable lateral CG limits? -- Correct: 700 lb (317 kg). CAUTION: imbalances in excess of 700 lb (317 kg) between fuel tanks, when combined with grossly unbalanced cargo/passenger loading, may put the aircraft outside of allowable lateral CG limits.
s92-lims-047.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I p.1-17, CAUTION preceding CABIN FLOOR LOADING LIMITS: 'Imbalances in excess of 700 pounds (317 kilograms) between fuel tanks, when combined with grossly unbalanced cargo/passenger loading, may put the aircraft outside of allowable lateral CG limits.' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-048.text: Per the PROPULSION AND DRIVE SYSTEM LIMITS notes, what happens if the aircraft is flown above 8,000 feet at outside air temperatures below -20°C and the corrected Ng speed limit is reached? -- Correct: The engine will not produce more power; further collective increase will only cause Nr to droop. "When flying at altitudes greater than 8,000 feet at outside air temperatures lower than -20 degrees C, it is possible to reach the corrected Ng speed limit of the engines. When this occurs, the engine will not produce more power. The only indication that the pilot will see when reaching this limit is that any further increase in collective will commensurately droop Nr."
s92-lims-048.note: RFM Part 1 Sec I PROPULSION AND DRIVE SYSTEM LIMITS p.1-18, table notes: 'When flying at altitudes greater than 8,000 feet at outside air temperatures lower than -20 degrees C, it is possible to reach the corrected Ng speed limit of the engines. When this occurs, the engine will not produce more power. The only indication...is that any further increase in collective will commensurately droop Nr.' Confirmed on the rendered page image.

s92-lims-049.text: What passenger seat limits apply to Category A and Category B operations? -- Correct: Category A: a maximum of 19 passenger seats. Category B: 9 or less. Types of operation: Category 'A' with a maximum of 19 passenger seats or Category 'B' with 9 or less passenger seats; Day, Night, VFR and IFR.
s92-lims-049.note: TYPES OF OPERATION p.1-1: Category A maximum 19 passenger seats, Category B 9 or less; Day, Night, VFR and IFR. (DOC 25) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-050.text: With the Rotor Ice Protection System (RIPS) installed, up to what altitude is flight in icing conditions approved? -- Correct: 10,000 feet pressure altitude. With the Rotor Ice Protection System (RIPS) installed, flight in icing conditions is approved up to 10,000 feet pressure altitude.
s92-lims-050.note: TYPES OF OPERATION p.1-1 (RIPS): flight in icing conditions up to 10,000 feet pressure altitude with RIPS installed. (DOC 25) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-051.text: Day or night VFR with degraded AFCS: which configuration still allows a maximum VNE of 165 KIAS? -- Correct: PSAS1 and PSAS2, AP1 and/or AP2, SAS mode, cyclic and rudder trim. Day or night VFR with certain PSAS and/or AP components inoperative: PSAS1 and PSAS2, AP1 or AP2, ATT mode — VNE 165 KIAS; PSAS1 and PSAS2, AP1 and/or AP2, SAS mode — VNE 165 KIAS; PSAS1 or PSAS2, AP1 and AP2, ATT mode — VNE 120 KIAS; PSAS1/AP1 or PSAS2/AP2, SAS mode with functional cyclic trim release — VNE 120 KIAS. Losing a PSAS channel is what drops VNE to 120 KIAS.
s92-lims-051.note: REQUIRED EQUIPMENT p.1-1 item 4, degraded VFR list: both PSAS with AP1 and/or AP2 in SAS mode 165 KIAS; single PSAS with both APs ATT 120; PSAS1/AP1 or PSAS2/AP2 SAS 120. (DOC 25) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-052.text: What does the RFM say about taking off with a secondary SAS engaged? -- Correct: It is not authorized; secondary SAS may be engaged after an inflight failure of a primary SAS computer. NOTE: takeoff with a secondary SAS engaged is not authorized. Secondary SAS may be engaged after an inflight failure of a primary SAS computer. CAUTION: when operating in a degraded AFCS mode, a pilot will be attentive to the flight controls when in ATT mode and will manually control the aircraft when flying in SAS mode.
s92-lims-052.note: REQUIRED EQUIPMENT p.1-2 NOTE: takeoff with secondary SAS engaged not authorized; secondary SAS may be engaged after inflight failure of a primary SAS computer. (DOC 26) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-053.text: In a degraded AFCS mode, what does the RFM CAUTION require of the pilot? -- Correct: Be attentive to the flight controls in ATT mode, and fly the aircraft manually in SAS mode. CAUTION: when operating in a degraded AFCS mode, a pilot will be attentive to the flight controls when in ATT mode and will manually control the aircraft when flying in SAS mode.
s92-lims-053.note: REQUIRED EQUIPMENT p.1-2 CAUTION: degraded AFCS mode, attentive to flight controls in ATT mode, manually control aircraft in SAS mode. (DOC 26) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-054.text: Which items on the required equipment list are required only for IMC? -- Correct: Two DCUs, two primary AC generators and all standby instruments. Required equipment: 1. Auxiliary power unit. 2. Two Data Concentrator Units (DCUs) (IMC). 3. Four instrument panel MFDs. 4. AFCS. 5. Two primary AC generators (IMC). 6. All standby instruments (IMC). 7. The applicable operators manual on board for all equipment not covered in Part II.
s92-lims-054.note: REQUIRED EQUIPMENT p.1-1/1-2: items marked (IMC): 2 two DCUs, 5 two primary AC generators, 6 all standby instruments; APU, MFDs and AFCS not marked IMC. (DOC 25, 26) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-055.text: In the S-92 RFM procedures, which seat does the "pilot" occupy, and where may the pilot in command sit? -- Correct: The pilot is in the right seat; the PIC may occupy either seat. Minimum flight crew: two pilots. For the procedures in this manual the "pilot" occupies the right cockpit seat and the "copilot" occupies the left cockpit seat. The Pilot in Command (PIC) may occupy either cockpit seat.
s92-lims-055.note: MINIMUM FLIGHT CREW p.1-2: two pilots; pilot right seat, copilot left seat; PIC may occupy either seat. (DOC 26) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-056.text: What does the RFM say about EGPWS and power lines? -- Correct: EGPWS gives no power line warnings; power lines are not in its database. The EGPWS will not provide power line warnings. Power lines are not included in the EGPWS data base.
s92-lims-056.note: EGPWS p.1-2: EGPWS will not provide power line warnings; power lines not included in the EGPWS data base. (DOC 26) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-057.text: When may EGPWS Low Altitude Mode be selected in IMC? -- Correct: Only as required for offshore platform IMC approaches or other Special Procedures. EGPWS Low Altitude Mode must not be selected when operating under IMC conditions except as required when performing offshore platform IMC Approach Procedures or other Special Procedures.
s92-lims-057.note: EGPWS p.1-2 item 2: Low Altitude Mode must not be selected in IMC except as required for offshore platform IMC Approach Procedures or other Special Procedures. (DOC 26) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-058.text: Beyond what latitudes must the pilot manually insert magnetic variation into the FMS? -- Correct: North of 73° N or south of 60° S. When operating north of 73 degrees north latitude or south of 60 degrees south latitude the pilot must manually insert magnetic variation.
s92-lims-058.note: FMS OPERATING LIMITATIONS p.1-3 item 5: north of 73° N or south of 60° S, manually insert magnetic variation. (DOC 28) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-059.text: If the air data input to the FMS is lost, what must the pilot do? -- Correct: Manually insert TAS and altitude every 10 minutes. When the air data input is lost to the FMS, the pilot must manually insert TAS and Altitude information every 10 minutes.
s92-lims-059.note: FMS OPERATING LIMITATIONS p.1-3 item 6: air data input lost, manually insert TAS and altitude every 10 minutes. (DOC 28) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-060.text: When are IFR en route and terminal navigation with the FMS prohibited? -- Correct: Unless the pilot verifies the database currency or checks each waypoint against current approved data. IFR En Route and Terminal navigation are prohibited unless the pilot verifies the currency of the data base or verifies each selected waypoint for accuracy by reference to current approved data. Other navigation equipment appropriate to the ground facilities along the route must be installed and operable as required by the operating rules.
s92-lims-060.note: FMS OPERATING LIMITATIONS p.1-4 item 7: IFR en route and terminal navigation prohibited unless pilot verifies database currency or verifies each selected waypoint against current approved data. (DOC 29) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-061.text: What limitations apply to FMS dead reckoning and to manually inserted runway coordinates? -- Correct: No navigation predicated on the FMS in dead reckoning; manually inserted runway coordinates are VFR only. FMS LNAV operation: navigation shall not be predicated upon the UNS-1Esp during periods of dead reckoning (DR). Following DR, position should be verified by sighting ground reference points and/or by other navigation equipment such as NDB, VOR, DME or radar fix. The use of manually inserted runway coordinates is limited to VFR operations.
s92-lims-061.note: FMS LNAV OPERATION p.1-4 items 1-3: no navigation predicated on UNS-1Esp during DR; verify position after DR; manually inserted runway coordinates limited to VFR. (DOC 29) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-062.text: If VNAV is to be used for an approach, when must en route VNAV be discontinued, and what is the primary altitude reference? -- Correct: Within 10 nm of the FAF; the pilot and copilot altimeters. If VNAV is to be used for approach, use of en route VNAV must be discontinued within 10 nm of the FAF. When the approach mode is activated, as indicated by a green APP on the PFD, VNAV may be armed for the approach. Pilot and copilot altimeters are the primary altitude reference during all VNAV operations.
s92-lims-062.note: FMS VNAV OPERATIONS p.1-4 items 1-2: discontinue en route VNAV within 10 nm of FAF; green APP then VNAV may be armed; pilot and copilot altimeters primary altitude reference. (DOC 29) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-063.text: An "INTEG" message appears on the PFD during an FMS approach. What does the RFM require? -- Correct: Discontinue navigation predicated on GPS. If an "INTEG" message is displayed on the PFD during an approach, navigation predicated on GPS should be discontinued. RAIM must be available at the final approach fix to accomplish GPS based non-precision approaches; when RAIM is not available, INTEG is displayed on the PFD and "NO GPS RAIM @ FAF" or "NO GPS @ MAP" messages on the CDU.
s92-lims-063.note: FMS APPROACHES p.1-4 items 3 and 5: INTEG on PFD during approach, discontinue GPS navigation; RAIM required at FAF for GPS non-precision approaches. (DOC 29) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-064.text: Which approach operations with the FMS are not approved or not authorized? -- Correct: GLS minimums and other WAAS operations, and ILS, LOC, LOC-BC, LDA, SDF and MLS approaches. FMS approaches: operation in accordance with GLS approach minimums and other operations requiring WAAS are not approved. ILS, LOC, LOC-BC, LDA, SDF and MLS approaches are not authorized. The UNS-1Esp is approved for FMS VFR approaches as a VFR pilot aid only. Instrument approaches must be conducted in the approach mode prior to the FAF, as indicated by a green APP on the PFD.
s92-lims-064.note: FMS APPROACHES p.1-4 items 6-8: GLS and WAAS operations not approved; ILS, LOC, LOC-BC, LDA, SDF, MLS approaches not authorized; FMS VFR approaches VFR pilot aid only. (DOC 29) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-065.text: Unless GPS approaches are approved for alternates by the operating rules, what must an alternate airport have? -- Correct: An approach based on other than GPS, with the aircraft equipment and navaid operational. Unless GPS approaches are approved for alternate airports by applicable operating rules, airports selected as alternates must be served by an approach based on other than GPS navigation. The aircraft must have operational equipment capable of using that navigation aid, and the required navigation aid must be operational.
s92-lims-065.note: FMS APPROACHES p.1-4A item 9: alternates must be served by a non-GPS approach unless operating rules approve GPS approaches for alternates; equipment and navaid operational. (DOC 30) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-066.text: Which of these is prohibited under the FLIGHT LIMITS? -- Correct: 360° hovering turns in less than 12 seconds. FLIGHT LIMITS: aerobatic maneuvers are prohibited; practice touchdown autorotations are prohibited; 360° hovering turns in less than 12 seconds are prohibited.
s92-lims-066.note: FLIGHT LIMITS p.1-5: 360° hovering turns in less than 12 seconds are prohibited. (DOC 31) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-067.text: Which icing conditions are prohibited, and what is required for flight into approved icing conditions? -- Correct: Freezing drizzle, freezing rain and SLD are prohibited; RIPS must be on for icing conditions. Flight in freezing drizzle/freezing rain/supercooled large drops (SLD) is prohibited. For flight into icing conditions, the Rotor Ice Protection System (RIPS) must be turned on.
s92-lims-067.note: FLIGHT LIMITS p.1-5: flight in freezing drizzle/freezing rain/SLD prohibited; for flight into icing conditions RIPS must be on. (DOC 31) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-068.text: When may the OEI engine power ratings be used? -- Correct: Only in the event of an actual engine failure. Use of OEI engine power ratings except in the event of an actual engine failure is prohibited.
s92-lims-068.note: FLIGHT LIMITS p.1-5: use of OEI engine power ratings except in the event of an actual engine failure is prohibited. (DOC 31) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-069.text: Which doors and windows may be open in flight? -- Correct: Cockpit windows if latched fully open, and the upper cabin door and lower SAR door with equipment secured. Flight with the ramp, airstair door or cabin windows open is prohibited. The opening of cockpit windows in flight is authorized provided the window can be latched fully open and loose equipment is secured in the cockpit. Flight with the upper cabin sliding door and the lower (inward opening) SAR door open is authorized provided loose equipment is secured in the cabin and applicable airspeed limits are observed.
s92-lims-069.note: FLIGHT LIMITS p.1-5: ramp, airstair door or cabin windows open prohibited; cockpit windows authorized if latched fully open and equipment secured; upper cabin sliding door and lower SAR door open authorized with loose equipment secured and airspeed limits observed. (DOC 31) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-070.text: What limits apply to opening or closing the upper sliding door in flight? -- Correct: 10° pitch up or down and 30° bank, with all occupants seated and belted or harnessed. Maximum pitch attitude for opening or closing the upper sliding door is 10° nose up or down, and maximum bank angle is 30°. CAUTION: prior to inflight operations with a cabin door open, all cabin occupants must be seated with a seat belt fastened or restrained with an approved and properly adjusted harness.
s92-lims-070.note: FLIGHT LIMITS p.1-5: upper sliding door opening/closing max pitch 10° nose up or down, max bank 30°; CAUTION occupants seated with belt or restrained by harness. (DOC 31) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-071.text: When is carriage of passengers prohibited? -- Correct: With the lower search/rescue door installed. Carriage of passengers is prohibited with the installation of the lower search/rescue door.
s92-lims-071.note: FLIGHT LIMITS p.1-5: carriage of passengers is prohibited with the installation of the lower search/rescue door. (DOC 31) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-072.text: What is the maximum demonstrated night Category A vertical Takeoff Decision Point (TDP)? -- Correct: 110 feet. Maximum demonstrated night Category A vertical Takeoff Decision Point (TDP) is 110 feet.
s92-lims-072.note: FLIGHT LIMITS p.1-5: maximum demonstrated night Category A vertical TDP is 110 feet. (DOC 31) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-073.text: What is the minimum helipad size for Category A ground level helipad operations? -- Correct: A 102 foot square. Category A ground level helipad takeoffs and landings are flown in accordance with the Category A procedures in Section II and within the weight, altitude and temperature limits of Section IV. Minimum helipad size for Category A ground level helipad operations is a 102 foot square.
s92-lims-073.note: FLIGHT LIMITS p.1-5: minimum helipad size for Category A ground level helipad operations is a 102 foot square. (DOC 31) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-074.text: When is flight within the avoid area of the height-velocity diagram authorized? -- Correct: During the Category A vertical ground level helipad takeoff and landing procedures, within their limits. Figure 1-1 (height-velocity diagram) NOTE: flight within the avoid area of the height-velocity diagram is authorized when conducting the Category A vertical ground level helipad takeoff and landing procedures described in Section II and when within the weight, altitude, temperature and wind limits for the applicable procedure.
s92-lims-074.note: Figure 1-1 Height-Velocity Diagram p.1-6 NOTE: flight within the avoid area authorized for Category A vertical ground level helipad procedures within their weight, altitude, temperature and wind limits. (DOC 32) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-075.text: On helicopters with the flotation system, what does the RFM say about the life rafts and floats in flight? -- Correct: Arming or deploying the life rafts and deploying the floats in flight are prohibited. FLIGHT LIMITS (FLOAT): arming or deploying the life rafts in flight is prohibited. Deploying the floats in flight is prohibited.
s92-lims-075.note: FLIGHT LIMITS continued p.1-7 (FLOAT): arming or deploying life rafts in flight prohibited; deploying floats in flight prohibited. (DOC 34) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-076.text: What are the maximum demonstrated IFR approach gradients? -- Correct: 4.0° above 90 KIAS; 7.0° at or below 90 KIAS. The maximum demonstrated IFR approach gradient for airspeeds above 90 KIAS is 4.0°. The maximum demonstrated IFR approach gradient for airspeeds at or below 90 KIAS is 7.0°.
s92-lims-076.note: FLIGHT LIMITS continued p.1-7: maximum demonstrated IFR approach gradient 4.0° above 90 KIAS, 7.0° at or below 90 KIAS. (DOC 34) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-077.text: What is VNE power on, and what calculates the VNE shown on the PFD? -- Correct: 165 KIAS; the air data computers, from temperature, pressure altitude and gross weight. VNE power on (maximum airspeed) is 165 KIAS. The air data computers automatically calculate VNE as a function of temperature, pressure altitude and gross weight for display on the airspeed indicator (PFD display mode).
s92-lims-077.note: AIRSPEED LIMITS p.1-7: VNE power on 165 KIAS; NOTE air data computers calculate VNE from temperature, pressure altitude and gross weight for the PFD. (DOC 34) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-078.text: What is the maximum airspeed with the landing gear down or in transit? -- Correct: 165 KIAS. Maximum airspeed with the landing gear down or in transit is 165 KIAS — the same as VNE power on. (The separate limit for activating the landing gear emergency blowdown is 90 KIAS.)
s92-lims-078.note: AIRSPEED LIMITS p.1-7: maximum airspeed with landing gear down or in transit 165 KIAS; emergency blowdown activation 90 KIAS. (DOC 34) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-079.text: Which of these conditions does NOT limit the airspeed to 120 KIAS? -- Correct: Landing gear down or in transit. Maximum airspeed is 120 KIAS with one engine inoperative, one or both SAS inoperative, both APs inoperative, one primary flight control servo inoperative, the hydraulic boost inoperative, or any sliding door or window pinned open. With the landing gear down or in transit the maximum is 165 KIAS.
s92-lims-079.note: AIRSPEED LIMITS p.1-7: 120 KIAS with one engine inop, one or both SAS inop, both APs inop, one primary servo inop, hydraulic boost inop, sliding door/window pinned open; gear down or in transit 165 KIAS. (DOC 34) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-080.text: What are the airspeed limits for flying with a sliding door or window pinned open, and for opening or closing it? -- Correct: 120 KIAS pinned open; 80 KIAS to open or close. Maximum airspeed with any sliding door or window pinned open is 120 KIAS. Maximum airspeed for opening or closing any sliding door or window is 80 KIAS. Both include the upper sliding SAR doors/windows, the inward opening lower door and the full length sliding door.
s92-lims-080.note: AIRSPEED LIMITS p.1-7: any sliding door or window pinned open 120 KIAS; opening or closing any sliding door or window 80 KIAS; includes upper SAR doors/windows, inward opening lower door, full length sliding door. (DOC 34) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-081.text: What is the maximum airspeed with the floats armed? -- Correct: 80 KIAS. (FLOAT) Maximum airspeed with floats armed is 80 KIAS. After an inadvertent float deployment the limits are 50 KIAS in a climb, 55 KIAS in level flight and 60 KIAS in descent/autorotation.
s92-lims-081.note: AIRSPEED LIMITS p.1-7 (FLOAT): maximum airspeed with floats armed 80 KIAS; after inadvertent deployment 50/55/60 KIAS. (DOC 34) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-082.text: What is the maximum groundspeed for a normal landing or takeoff, and what follows a landing above it? -- Correct: 50 knots; after landing faster, further flight and towing are prohibited, but taxiing is permitted. Temporary Revision No. 3 (facing page 1-7) changes the limit to: maximum groundspeed for normal landing or takeoff is 50 knots (the basic page still shows 65 knots). NOTE: after landing in excess of 50 knots groundspeed, further flight and towing is prohibited. Taxi operations are permitted.
s92-lims-082.note: Temporary Revision No. 3 (DOC 33, facing p.1-7): maximum groundspeed for normal landing or takeoff 50 knots, replacing 65 knots on p.1-7; NOTE after landing above 50 knots groundspeed further flight and towing prohibited, taxi permitted. (DOC 33, 34) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-083.text: What is Vmini, the minimum airspeed for instrument flight? -- Correct: 50 KIAS. Vmini (minimum airspeed for instrument flight) is 50 KIAS.
s92-lims-083.note: AIRSPEED LIMITS p.1-7: Vmini (minimum airspeed for instrument flight) is 50 KIAS. (DOC 34) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-084.text: What are the maximum airspeeds for windshield wiper operation? -- Correct: Standard wiper 40 knots; improved wiper 100 KIAS. Maximum airspeed for standard windshield wiper operations is 40 knots. Maximum airspeed for improved windshield wiper operations is 100 KIAS. The improved wiper arm has a stiffener inside the "U", visible from the cockpit.
s92-lims-084.note: AIRSPEED LIMITS p.1-8: standard windshield wiper 40 knots; improved wiper 100 KIAS; NOTE improved arm has stiffener inside the U. (DOC 35) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-085.text: What are the limits for sideward flight or crosswind hover, and for rearward flight or tailwind hover? -- Correct: 35 knots for both. Maximum airspeed for sideward flight or crosswind hover is 35 knots. Maximum airspeed for rearward flight or tailwind hover is 35 knots.
s92-lims-085.note: AIRSPEED LIMITS p.1-8: sideward flight or crosswind hover 35 knots; rearward flight or tailwind hover 35 knots. (DOC 35) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-086.text: What is the maximum altitude for Category A ground level helipad operations? -- Correct: 5,500 feet density altitude or 6,000 feet pressure altitude, whichever is lower. Maximum altitude for Category A ground level helipad operations is 5,500 feet density altitude or 6,000 feet pressure altitude, whichever is lower.
s92-lims-086.note: ALTITUDE LIMITS p.1-8: Category A ground level helipad operations maximum 5,500 ft density altitude or 6,000 ft pressure altitude, whichever is lower. (DOC 35) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-087.text: What are the minimum altitudes for coupled operations? -- Correct: 200 feet AGL above 120 KIAS; 50 feet AGL at or below 120 KIAS. Minimum altitude for coupled operations with airspeed above 120 KIAS is 200 feet AGL. Minimum altitude for coupled operations with airspeed at or below 120 KIAS is 50 feet AGL.
s92-lims-087.note: ALTITUDE LIMITS p.1-8: coupled operations minimum 200 ft AGL above 120 KIAS, 50 ft AGL at or below 120 KIAS. (DOC 35) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-088.text: What applies to coupled flight at low height? -- Correct: Below 200 feet AGL the pilot monitors the controls; below 100 feet AGL it must be in VMC. When coupled below 200 feet AGL, the pilot will monitor the flight controls and take action in the event of an excessive rate of descent. Coupled flight below 100 feet AGL will be in visual meteorological conditions.
s92-lims-088.note: ALTITUDE LIMITS p.1-8: coupled below 200 ft AGL pilot monitors flight controls and acts on excessive rate of descent; coupled below 100 ft AGL in VMC. (DOC 35) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-089.text: When is operation prohibited because of cold soaking, and how is airworthy status restored? -- Correct: Engines shut down below -25°C for over 1 hour; warm at 0°C or above for 8 hours, or use the pre-heat kit. Operation is prohibited if the rotorcraft, with its engines shut down, is exposed to a ground ambient temperature below -25°C for a period longer than 1 hour. To restore airworthy status it should be warmed at or above 0°C (+32°F) for 8 hours, or the Cold Weather Pre-heat kit (P/N 92700-00110-011) must be used in accordance with the RFM Cold Weather Procedures.
s92-lims-089.note: AMBIENT TEMPERATURE LIMITS p.1-8: prohibited if exposed with engines shut down below -25°C for longer than 1 hour; restore by warming at or above 0°C for 8 hours or pre-heat kit per Cold Weather Procedures. (DOC 35) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-090.text: Below what OAT should pitot heat and engine anti-ice be turned on? -- Correct: Below 5°C. Pitot heat and engine anti-ice should be turned on when OAT is less than 5°C.
s92-lims-090.note: AMBIENT TEMPERATURE LIMITS p.1-8: pitot heat and engine anti-ice on when OAT is less than 5°C. (DOC 35) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-091.text: What are the ECS limits for cockpit ventilation in flight? -- Correct: No MAX ACS or recirculation in flight (MAX ACS on the ground only); cockpit vent on if no heat or AC. To assure adequate fresh air ventilation to the cockpit when operating the air-conditioning system in flight, the cockpit temperature mode selection switch shall not be placed in the MAX ACS or recirculation position. The air-conditioning MAX ACS position is to be used on the ground only. If neither heat nor air-conditioning is used in flight, the cockpit vent must be on.
s92-lims-091.note: ENVIRONMENTAL CONTROL SYSTEM LIMITS p.1-8: in flight no MAX ACS or recirculation; MAX ACS ground only; if neither heat nor AC in flight, cockpit vent must be on. (DOC 35) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-092.text: What is the minimum operating weight of the S-92? -- Correct: 16,200 pounds (7,348 kg). Maximum takeoff and landing weight is 26,500 pounds (12,020 kg). Minimum operating weight is 16,200 pounds (7,348 kg). The helicopter is to be operated using the approved loading schedule (LOADING INFORMATION, RFM Part 2, Section II).
s92-lims-092.note: WEIGHT LIMITS p.1-9: maximum takeoff and landing 26,500 lb (12,020 kg); minimum operating weight 16,200 lb (7,348 kg). (DOC 36) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-093.text: On the Category A takeoff and landing gross weight charts, what is the minimum TDP speed with a crosswind component greater than 20 knots? -- Correct: 45 KIAS. Figure 1-2 (Cat 'A' Takeoff and Landing Gross Weight, all sheets) NOTE: with a crosswind component greater than 20 kts, the minimum TDP speed is 45 KIAS. The charts apply to 35 knots of crosswind component or less.
s92-lims-093.note: Figure 1-2 sheets 1-4 (p.1-10, 1-11, 1-12, 1-12A) NOTE: with a crosswind component greater than 20 kts, the minimum TDP speed is 45 KIAS; charts titled 35 knots of crosswind component or less. (DOC 37, 38, 39, 40) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-094.text: The 30 minute dual engine rating (100% Q, 988°C TGT) applies to which flight condition? -- Correct: Hovering flight only. CT7-8A propulsion and drive system limits: 30 MIN rating, 30 minutes, 100% Q, 988°C TGT, 101.5% Ng. Note (2): the rating applies to hovering flight only.
s92-lims-094.note: PROPULSION AND DRIVE SYSTEM LIMITS table p.1-18: 30 MIN (2) 30 MIN, 100% Q, TGT 988, Ng 101.5; note (2) rating applies to hovering flight only. (DOC 46) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-095.text: What are the single engine maximum continuous and 2 minute OEI torque and TGT limits? -- Correct: Both 120% Q; TGT 988°C maximum continuous and 1006°C for 2 minutes. Single engine limits: maximum continuous 120% Q, 988°C TGT, 102.4% Ng; OEI 2 minutes 120% Q, 1006°C TGT, 102.9% Ng; OEI 30 seconds 141% Q, 1049°C TGT, 103.7% Ng.
s92-lims-095.note: PROPULSION AND DRIVE SYSTEM LIMITS table p.1-18, single engine: MCP 120% Q, 988°C, 102.4% Ng; OEI 2 MIN 120% Q, 1006°C, 102.9% Ng; OEI 30 SEC 141% Q, 1049°C. (DOC 46) Checked on the rendered page image 2026-09-25.

s92-lims-096.text: What are the transient torque limits, dual engine and single engine? -- Correct: Dual engine 120% for 10 seconds; single engine 156% for 5 seconds. Transient torque: dual engine 120% for 10 seconds; single engine 156% for 5 seconds. Note (3): these are associated with torque ramp up due to abnormal rotor droop at the FADEC controlled dual engine or OEI limit.

s92-lims-097.text: What are the dual engine transient TGT limit and the maximum starting TGT? -- Correct: 1003°C for 12 seconds; 1000°C peak during start. Dual engine TRANSIENT, 12 seconds: TGT 1003°C, Ng 103.7%, Np 116%. MAX. STARTING: peak TGT 1000°C.
